final_answer: Depth-first search (DFS) and breadth-first search (BFS) differ in traversal order and memory usage. DFS explores as far as possible along branches before backtracking, using a stack (or recursion). BFS explores all neighbors level by level, using a queue. DFS finds paths quickly in deep graphs, while BFS guarantees the shortest path in unweighted graphs. Choose DFS for puzzles/mazes or memory constraints; use BFS for shortest-path problems or when exploring shallow layers first.
